final_text:
## Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence reviewed:** `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames, 623.9 s capture). No IDS/Suricata alert export or other artifacts were present alongside the pcap — this analysis is network-evidence only.

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | Dominant local host in all suspicious conversations |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** | ARP (`10.1.21.58 → 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2`), confirmed by DHCP request |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (domain member of **WIN11OFFICE** / dual-suffix `mshome.net`) | NBNS, DHCP option 12 |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos `CNameString`, seen from both 10.1.21.58 and the DC 10.1.21.2 |

### Malware family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS alerts were provided, and the payload itself was transferred entirely inside TLS, so no file could be extracted or hashed from this capture.

The traffic is consistent with a **fingerprinting-gated malware delivery chain** (a "TDS"/anti-bot gate feeding a fake-file-host payload drop), a pattern commonly used by ClickFix/FakeCaptcha-style stealer and loader campaigns:

1. `hiyter.com` (t=45.3s) — initial lure/redirector.
2. `media.megafilehub4.lat` (t=45.8s) and `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (t=48.3s) — fake file-hosting domains; the client pulled a **16 MB payload over TLS** from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67) between t=48–70s.
3. `whooptm.cyou` (t=90.3s) and `whitepepper.su` (t=92–103s) — a browser-fingerprinting/anti-analysis gate. The host made repeated `GET`/`POST /api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b` requests, once claiming `agent=Chrome` and again seconds later claiming `agent=Edge` with the same id/token, each POST uploading a full browser/hardware fingerprint (canvas hash, WebGL renderer, installed fonts, screen/hardware specs). This same-id-different-UA pattern in seconds is consistent with automated fingerprint collection by the dropped payload, not organic user browsing.
4. `holiday-forever.cc` (t=122.8s) and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (t=126.5s) — additional one-time redirector/gate check-ins.

No sustained periodic beaconing was observed for the rest of the 623-second capture, so this looks like a single infection/gate-check sequence rather than an established, persistent C2 loop within this capture window.

### Indicators of Compromise

**Malicious domains**
| Domain | Role |
|---|---|
| hiyter.com | initial redirector/lure |
| media.megafilehub4.lat | fake file-hosting portal |
| arch.filemegahab4.sbs | fake file-hosting portal, served 16 MB payload over TLS |
| whooptm.cyou | fingerprinting gate |
| whitepepper.su | fingerprinting gate (`/api/set_agent`) |
| holiday-forever.cc | secondary redirector/gate |
| communicationfirewall-security.cc | secondary redirector/gate |

**C2/gate endpoints (IP:port)**
| Endpoint | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 153.92.1.49:80 | plaintext HTTP `GET/POST /api/set_agent` to whitepepper.su, followed in `tshark -z follow,tcp` |
| 153.92.1.49:443 | additional TLS sessions to whitepepper.su (same host) |
| 80.97.160.24:443 | TLS ClientHello SNI=holiday-forever.cc |
| 62.72.32.156:443 | TLS ClientHello SNI=whooptm.cyou |
| 104.21.46.67:443 (Cloudflare edge, shared IP) | TLS ClientHello SNI=arch.filemegahab4.sbs, 16 MB transferred |
| 104.21.48.156:443 (Cloudflare edge, shared IP) | TLS ClientHello SNI=media.megafilehub4.lat |
| 104.21.9.36:443 (Cloudflare edge, shared IP) | TLS ClientHello SNI=communicationfirewall-security.cc |
| 104.21.22.231:443 (Cloudflare edge, shared IP) | TLS ClientHello SNI=hiyter.com |

**Malicious URL**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b` — fingerprint-gate check-in endpoint, seen with `agent=Chrome` and `agent=Edge` variants and `&act=log` POST.

**Transferred file / hash**
- None extractable. The 16 MB object from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` was carried inside TLS and cannot be recovered or hashed from this capture. No plaintext-HTTP-delivered executable exists in this pcap.

### Benign context (not indicators)
Active Directory/domain background noise for WIN11OFFICE/mshome.net (NBNS, WPAD, LDAP, Kerberos, SMB2/SAMR/LSARPC, DC 10.1.21.2), Microsoft telemetry and services (edge.microsoft.com, msn.com, officeapps.live.com, login.microsoftonline.com, watson/events.data.microsoft.com, msftconnecttest.com NCSI check), Google services (accounts/googleapis/gstatic/youtube/safebrowsing/mtalk), Bing, Skype config, cdnjs.cloudflare.com, static.cloudflareinsights.com, assets.adobedtm.com.

### Summary
Windows workstation **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (10.1.21.58, MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2), logged in as **gwyatt**, was infected via a fake file-download portal chain (`hiyter.com` → `media.megafilehub4.lat`/`arch.filemegahab4.sbs`), pulling a 16 MB payload over TLS. The infection then checked in to a browser-fingerprinting gate (`whooptm.cyou`, `whitepepper.su`) and two further redirector domains (`holiday-forever.cc`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`). No IDS signature or extractable payload was available, so the specific malware family cannot be named with certainty — attribution here is behavioral, based on the fake-file-host + fingerprint-gate delivery pattern typical of commodity stealer/loader campaigns.
